title: Yaga Renewed for Season 2 as Carrie-Anne Moss Confirms Her Return
excerpt:
Canadian streamer Crave has ordered a second season of the mystery thriller Yaga.
Carrie-Anne Moss is confirmed to return, while the rest of the cast remains unannounced.
body_md:
Canadian streaming service Crave has renewed the mystery thriller Yaga for a second season before the first season has finished its run. Carrie-Anne Moss, known worldwide for The Matrix films, is confirmed to return. At the time of the announcement, however, no other cast member had been formally confirmed for the new season, an important distinction for a series built around an ensemble of suspicious characters.

Yaga premiered on Crave on October 23, 2026, and its first season is heading toward a two-episode finale on AMC+ in the United States on November 27. The renewal follows a strong launch: the series led Crave's opening-weekend rankings and was reported as AMC+'s top series launch. It has also performed prominently on services in India, Australia and New Zealand. Those rankings signal interest, although the companies have not disclosed a comprehensive worldwide audience figure.

The series draws on the Slavic legend of Baba Yaga, recasting the folklore within a contemporary missing-person mystery. The disappearance of Henry Park, a privileged heir to a commercial fishing business, sets the plot in motion. Private investigator Charlie Rapp is hired to find him, and attention increasingly turns toward Dr. Katherine Hargrove, a university professor surrounded by unsettling rumors. The premise blends investigative suspense with questions about the stories people tell about women, power and danger.

Hudson Williams, also known for Heated Rivalry, plays Henry Park. Noah Reid portrays Charlie Rapp, while Moss plays Dr. Hargrove. Clark Backo is another prominent member of the first-season cast. Their presence in the existing episodes does not establish their participation in season two. The renewal announcement specifically identifies Moss as returning, and further casting details will have to come from the producers.

Kat Sandler developed the television series from her own stage play and serves as writer, showrunner and executive producer. Blink49 Studios and Front Street Pictures produce in association with Bell Media. Moss also holds an executive producer credit, alongside Mackenzie Donaldson and Andrew Miller, with Charles Cooper producing. International distribution is handled by Sphere Abacus.

The first season has reached audiences beyond Canada through AMC+ in the United States, Sky and Now in the United Kingdom and Ireland, HBO Max in parts of Europe, BINGE and Foxtel in Australia, Neon in New Zealand, and Lionsgate Play in India. A Brazilian release through Globo is planned for 2027. These arrangements describe the first season's international footprint; they should not be taken as a confirmed release plan for season two.

Bell Media executive Justin Stockman welcomed the audience response and praised the production partners following the renewal. The creative team now has the opportunity to continue the show's world, but a second-season premiere date, episode count, production schedule and plot synopsis have not yet been announced. For now, the confirmed development is the renewal itself and Moss's return, rather than any specific prediction about how the mystery will evolve.
